verdict.root_cause: checkout is crashing inside its own request path: a nil-pointer dereference (SIGSEGV) raised in sendToPostProcessor (main.go:630) under PlaceOrder (main.go:388) on gRPC-served requests, panicking twice at 22:59 and then going silent in the log store while still intermittently failing PlaceOrder with a fast, self-attributed error that names a shipping-quote and an email 400 with no corresponding child spans [tr_58ffbe0e4fc5][tr_641900452056]. The failures are fast, intermittent and originate in checkout's own span self-time, not in any dependency, and the error ratio shifted abruptly at ~23:39 rather than creeping up [tr_d6f9ed35aa55][tr_641900452056]. The change log for checkout holds nothing, but the queried window starts at onset and only covers the seed service, so a pre-onset change is unexcluded [tr_2d84fe3c5698][tr_3f2c9028e057]. An empty change record plus a fast, self-generated error naming a code path that never made the call it reports is the signature of a runtime flag flipping checkout onto a broken branch; the running artifact itself is not shown to be wrong.
verdict.reasoning: Traces put the error in checkout's own span with no ERROR child and no email/shipping spans at all, which rules out dependency propagation and latency cascade [tr_641900452056]. Logs show the mechanism is an in-process nil dereference on checkout's PlaceOrder path, with no dependency, decode, connection or OOM signatures, ruling out datastore_corruption, resource_exhaustion and network-level causes [tr_58ffbe0e4fc5]. Failure is fast (11.1ms span) and intermittent, not hanging, which excludes process_freeze and network_partition — both of which also require caller hangs rather than fast errors [tr_641900452056][tr_d6f9ed35aa55]. Change history for checkout is empty [tr_2d84fe3c5698][tr_3f2c9028e057]; per the taxonomy, an empty change log with fast errors and a span-carried error message is the feature_flag signature rather than evidence against a change-shaped fault. The ratio moved abruptly at a single change point rather than drifting, consistent with a value flipping at runtime [tr_d6f9ed35aa55].
open_questions: No flag store or flag-daemon evidence was ever pulled; the feature_flag attribution rests on absence of a change record plus fault shape, not on an observed flag flip.
The change query covered only checkout from onset forward — a deploy or config edit landing shortly before 23:40:31, or on a dependency, remains unexamined [tr_2d84fe3c5698][tr_3f2c9028e057].

The two metric pulls disagree: one shows a 1.82x rise with a change point at 23:39:31, the other shows the ratio slightly below baseline with a change point at 23:41:31 [tr_d6f9ed35aa55][tr_c24b7542b607]. No request-rate or p95 series was ever returned.
The 22:59 panics are ~41 minutes before the 23:40:31 alert and checkout logged nothing after; whether checkout was restarted, crashlooping, or silently running between those points is unsettled.
Why the error string names an email 400 when no email span exists is unexplained [tr_641900452056].

alternatives.root_cause: A checkout build or artifact change shortly before onset introduced the nil-pointer path in sendToPostProcessor, making the running artifact the wrong one.
alternatives.why_not: The change query that would show a deploy never covered the pre-onset hours and no image change is on record [tr_2d84fe3c5698][tr_3f2c9028e057]; with no prior tag recorded, rollback's precondition is unmet. A code-level panic is equally consistent with a flag steering into existing broken code.

alternatives.root_cause: checkout's process died at the second panic and never came back, so callers saw it stop answering and the 23:40:31 alerts are the cascade.
alternatives.why_not: checkout was still serving — three complete, error-free PlaceOrder traces at 23:36 and a continuous ratio series with a non-zero denominator [tr_641900452056][tr_c24b7542b607] — and failures are fast errors, not hangs, which a freeze does not produce.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so nothing in the system should change: checkout's error ratio stays at its current bursty, intermittent level (mean ~0.028, max 0.5, minimum still touching zero) and PlaceOrder continues to fail a minority of requests fast [tr_d6f9ed35aa55][tr_641900452056]. The next observable step is evidence, not remediation: (a) a flag-store / flag-daemon read to see whether a flag governing checkout's sendToPostProcessor branch was actually flipped near 23:39, (b) a change-history query on checkout covering the hours *before* 23:40:31 and extending to checkout's dependencies, since the executed query started at onset and covered only the seed service [tr_2d84fe3c5698][tr_3f2c9028e057], and (c) a calls_total and p95 series for checkout to settle which of the two contradictory error-ratio pulls describes the window [tr_d6f9ed35aa55][tr_c24b7542b607].
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the missing evidence arrives and meets an action's preconditions: a flag record showing a flip on a checkout-read flag at ~23:39 would make revert_config the correct proposal, and a pre-onset deploy or image-tag change on checkout would make rollback_image correct. It is also wrong if checkout is observed to be crashlooping — a startup banner repeating in the log store, or a container restart count climbing — because that is process state and would support restart_service. Right now none of those observations exist: no flag evidence was ever pulled, the change window never covered the pre-onset hours, and checkout emitted no log line at all after 22:59:33, so whether it restarted, crashlooped, or ran silently is unobserved [tr_58ffbe0e4fc5]. The cost of abstaining is that the intermittent PlaceOrder failures continue meanwhile; that is visible as a continuing non-zero error ratio and is the thing to weigh against acting blind.
proposal.risk: The risk of the action I am declining to propose is the reason for declining. revert_config on checkout would recreate the container with its declared environment — but the feature_flag mechanism lives in the flag daemon's bind-mounted file, not in checkout's environment, so a config revert would recreate checkout without touching the flag and would be mistaken for a null result rather than a wrong diagnosis. If the real mechanism is instead a bad artifact (the nil dereference at main.go:630 is in checkout's own compiled code [tr_58ffbe0e4fc5]), reverting config leaves the broken binary running while consuming an approval and resetting the incident clock. A restart carries a further, irreversible cost: it discards in-process cache and destroys whatever process state would have distinguished crashloop from silent-but-running, which is one of the open questions.
proposal.blast_radius: Nothing changes, so nobody sees anything. For contrast, had an action been proposed against checkout, its inbound callers in this incident — frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator, all already alerting — would have seen connection resets for the duration of the container recreate, and checkout's downstream set (cart, currency, payment, product-catalog, shipping, email) would have seen a traffic gap during the same interval.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical simultaneous alerts across checkout, frontend and the proxy plus the load generator describe a user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed, and no open incident covers it. The seed set spans the whole request path with many unmeasured downstream edges, so no fault class is suggested yet.
